images.caption: Beam Engine housing Now ruined, this building was part of a beam engine housing. It was built to drain the local pits in the 18th century. It was later reused as a doocot. A full size working beam engine can be seen in the National Museum of Scotland, Edinburgh.

images.caption: Boness Health Centre Built in 1981 in the grounds of Boness Hospital this Health Centre is used by 2 of the 3 Family Doctor practices in the town.  It is also a base for District Nurses, Health Visitors, Physiotherapy, Podiatry and an X-ray unit. A treatment room allows for dressings and minor surgery to save patients travelling to District General Hospitals several miles away.

images.caption: Boness Public Primary School One of several primary schools in the town The Public suffered a few years ago when the local authority in an exercise of political correctness ruled that the word Public be stricken from the name of all schools in their area with no substitution added. Several schools in towns in the district suffered chaos as Post Offices and other delivery contractors struggled to find which school was meant on the labels.  The ruling was soon rescinded. The cost in late deliveries and printing of stationery etc was not made - er -  public.

images.caption:
Arthur's Seat, Edinburgh, viewed from Pollock Halls.  
1880s map of the park
Arthur's Seat, an extinct volcano and the highest point in Edinburgh, is at the centre of the park, with the cliffs of Salisbury Crags to the west. There are three lochs: St Margaret's Loch, Dunsapie Loch, and Duddingston Loch. The ruins of St Anthony's Chapel stand above St Margaret's Loch. Queen's Drive is the main route through the Park. St Margaret's Well and St Anthony's Well are both natural springs within the park. Holyrood Park is located to the south-east of the Old Town, at the edge of the city centre. Abbeyhill is to the north, and Duddingston village to the east. The University of Edinburgh's Pollock Halls of Residence are to the south-west, and Dumbiedykes is to the west.
Arthur's Seat is the remains of a now extinct volcano which rises 250 metres (823 feet) above Holyrood Park in Edinburgh.
